newsitem.title: USA: GM launches production of bi-fuel trucks.
newsitem.headline: GM launches production of bi-fuel trucks.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Wednesday it will produce "bi-fuel" full-size pickup trucks that can run on both compressed natural gas or gasoline during the 1997 model year.
The bi-fuel compressed natural gas option will carry a $5,800 price, over the normal prices for the Chevrolet C2500 and GMC Sierra trucks. The option is aimed at fleet buyers.
The trucks will use a Vortec 5700 V-8 engine specifically modified to burn natural gas, and will be equipped with a carbon-fiber wrapped steel tank for the compressed natural gas.

The tanks and other components are being provided by IMPCO Technologies, a unit of Air Sensors Inc. GM turned to IMPCO to develop new technology for such systems a few years ago when gas tanks burst on GM trucks using previous technology.
